title: Remove Baskets from Inactive Customers
prompt: You are working with an online grocery service that tracks shopping baskets and customer reorder behavior. The service wants to delete all shopping baskets that belong to customers whose account status is 'inactive'. Write a single DELETE statement that removes these baskets by joining to the customers table. After the deletion, confirm the remaining rows with a SELECT statement ordered by basket_id.

display.context: You are working with an online grocery service that tracks shopping baskets and customer reorder behavior.
display.task: Write a query that deletes all shopping baskets belonging to customers whose account status is 'inactive', then returns the remaining baskets.

table_notes.shopping_baskets: holds each customer's current shopping basket with items and total value
table_notes.customers: holds customer account information including their current status

output_field_notes.basket_id: unique identifier for each shopping basket
output_field_notes.item_count: how many items are in the basket
output_field_notes.total_value: total dollar value of the basket

edge_cases: If a customer has status 'inactive', their basket is removed regardless of basket value or item count.
If a customer has any other status, their basket is kept.
display.filter_note: only baskets whose customer_id links to a customer with status = 'inactive' are deleted
display.order_by_note: the remaining baskets are ordered by basket_id ascending

schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE customers (customer_id INT PRIMARY KEY, customer_name VARCHAR(100), email VARCHAR(100), account_status VARCHAR(20), last_order_date DATE); CREATE TABLE shopping_baskets (basket_id INT PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INT, item_count INT, total_value DECIMAL(10,2), created_at TIMESTAMP);
example_input_data: INSERT INTO customers (customer_id, customer_name, email, account_status, last_order_date) VALUES (101, 'Alice Thompson', 'alice@example.com', 'active', '2024-03-15'), (102, 'Bob Martinez', 'bob@example.com', 'inactive', '2023-11-20'), (103, 'Carol Lee', 'carol@example.com', 'active', '2024-03-10'), (104, 'David Chen', 'david@example.com', 'inactive', '2023-09-05'), (105, 'Emma Wilson', 'emma@example.com', 'pending', '2024-03-01'), (106, 'Frank Rodriguez', 'frank@example.com', 'active', '2024-03-18'); INSERT INTO shopping_baskets (basket_id, customer_id, item_count, total_value, created_at) VALUES (1001, 101, 5, 47.50, '2024-03-18 10:30:00'), (1002, 102, 3, 22.00, '2024-03-17 14:15:00'), (1003, 103, 8, 95.75, '2024-03-18 09:00:00'), (1004, 104, 2, 15.50, '2024-03-16 16:45:00'), (1005, 105, 4, 38.25, '2024-03-18 11:20:00'), (1006, 106, 6, 72.00, '2024-03-18 13:10:00');

composite_moves: join shopping_baskets to customers on customer_id
select remaining rows ordered by basket_id

hints: You need to reference both the shopping_baskets table and the customers table to check the account status.
Use the USING clause to join the customers table in your DELETE statement, matching on customer_id.
In your WHERE clause, filter to customers where account_status equals 'inactive', then follow with a SELECT statement to show the remaining baskets ordered by basket_id.
answer_key: DELETE FROM shopping_baskets USING customers WHERE shopping_baskets.customer_id = customers.customer_id AND customers.account_status = 'inactive'; SELECT * FROM shopping_baskets ORDER BY basket_id;
